title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
statement: In an n x n grid of 0s (open) and 1s (blocked), find the length of the shortest path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell moving through open cells in any of 8 directions. The length counts cells on the path (including both ends). Return -1 if no path exists.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    return [[[0] * 200 for _ in range(200)]]

hints.1_question: You want the fewest steps in an unweighted grid. Which traversal gives shortest paths?
hints.2_nudge: BFS from the top-left, moving in all 8 directions through 0-cells, tracking the number of cells on the path. Check that start and end are open first.
hints.3_big_hint: If grid[0][0] or grid[n-1][n-1] is 1 return -1. Queue (r, c, 1); mark visited when enqueued; return d at the target; otherwise -1.

known_bugs.name: only 4 directions
known_bugs.followup: The statement allows moves in 8 directions. Which do you try?

known_bugs.name: counts steps (edges) instead of cells
known_bugs.followup: In a 1 x 1 grid the path has one cell. What length do you report?

known_bugs.name: does not check whether the start/end cells are blocked
known_bugs.followup: What if the top-left cell itself is blocked?

followups: Why is marking visited at enqueue time important for speed?
